properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardcoded 32-byte secp256k1 ECDSA private keys for the "Alice" and "Carol" CI test accounts in the fhevm end-to-end encrypted-ERC20 CI test. Consumed at ci/tests/ERC20.py:117/123 via Account.from_key and construct_sign_and_send_raw_middleware (raw transaction signing). Test-fixture accounts, not production credentials — but real committed key material; the same repo also commits a deployer key in .env.example:3. Changeable here (rotate/regenerate test accounts).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves 1.4.2 (pulled into package-lock.json via the hardhat/ethereumjs/ethers toolchain — e.g. node_modules/@ethereumjs/util/node_modules/@noble/curves) provides secp256k1 ECDSA, the curve Ethereum transaction signing runs on. Available in the shipped library; the repo's own first-party signing goes through ethers/eth_account instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped-library surface: @noble/curves 1.4.2 also ships secp256r1 (P-256) ECDSA/ECDH. No first-party call site selects P-256 in this repo; the image ships the capability through the hardhat/ethereumjs toolchain regardless.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic 6.6.1 sits in the hardhat/ethereumjs dependency tree and provides ECDH (and ECDSA) over secp256k1/P-256. No direct first-party call site; reachable transitively (e.g. older ethereumjs components). Classic-EC key agreement, retroactively breakable — the highest-priority PQ migration class.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PyNaCl X25519 declared for the CI Python stack. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's pre-standard SHA-3) is the repo's pervasive hash. Live sites in this object: EIP-712 message hashing at ci/tests/ERC20.py:73 (pysha3 keccak_256 over eip712-structs signable_bytes, AST-confirmed) and ciphertext-handle hashing at test/fhevmjsMocked.ts:354/365 (sha3 npm Keccak(256)), plus keccak/@ethersproject/keccak256 dependency entries. The adjacent completing operation at ERC20.py:74 — msg_sig = account.signHash(msg_hash) — signs that hash with secp256k1 ECDSA via eth_acc

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes 1.4.0 (pulled by @noble/curves via the ethereumjs stack) ships keccak/sha3 among its hash suite. No direct first-party import; available in the shipped library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The authenticated-encryption half of PyNaCl's crypto_box_seal. Live use in the re-encryption flow at ci/tests/ERC20.py:94-95 (SealedBox(sk).decrypt(box)) — the CI test decrypts its re-encrypted token balance with it. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The elliptic-curve library inside the hardhat/ethereumjs toolchain: @noble/curves ships secp256k1, P-256, X25519, ed25519 and more, and is what ethers v6 and ethereumjs use for Ethereum signing math. Root package.json/package-lock.json declarations; used transitively by the repo's own toolchain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: requests 2.32.2 is the CI Python stack's HTTP client; its TLS posture (urllib3/OpenSSL defaults of the CI image, no pinning or explicit cipher config anywhere in-repo) governs CI egress HTTPS — e.g. py-solc-x fetching solc binaries and web3 HTTPProvider calls. tls_sessions found no explicitly-configured TLS session in this tree, so this default posture is the asset. Observable here, fixed by the requests/urllib3 versions the CI image installs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Node crypto.randomBytes(32) — the CSPRNG — generating 32 random bytes appended to simulated ciphertexts to mimic TFHE encryption noise in the mocked fhevm instance (test fixture). Secure randomness, correct choice; the same CSPRNG class is used at test/coprocessorUtils.ts:97 and test/fhevmOperations/fhevmRevertPaths.ts:21/30/39 (reported separately).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PyNaCl 1.5.0 (libsodium binding) is the CI Python crypto library: X25519 (used live in the re-encryption flow), Ed25519, XSalsa20-Poly1305, Argon2id and a CSPRNG all ship in it. Declared in ci/requirements.txt, imported and used in ci/tests/ERC20.py.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.6.1 — legacy EC library in the hardhat/ethereumjs dependency tree; ships secp256k1/P-256 curves with ECDSA/ECDH. No direct first-party import; the toolchain (older ethereumjs components) reaches it. Shipped-library presence.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: requests 2.32.2 — the declared CI HTTP client; its TLS posture is the separate ALG-01b51b8d object, this entry records the package itself. Used by the CI scripts (and transitively by py-solc-x) for outbound HTTP(S).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Browser pbkdf2 package (3.1.2) in the hardhat/ethereumjs dependency tree — the classic browserify-style PBKDF2 used by wallet libraries for BIP-39 seed derivation (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512). No direct first-party import; shipped-library capability, and the PBKDF2 object ALG-4de3b020 (scout 1's shard) records the algorithm entries.
